output.name: Nelu

anatomy.part: bottom corner of the kite, where the tail hangs
right corner of the kite, where the flying string is tied
the salt token at the crossing of the kite's spars
lantern at the masthead of the far boat

output.myth: When Ennu the Kite-Wright was still green at the work, he built a kite to carry a bargain across rough water. The boats of the north and the boats of the south could not row to meet. So Ennu sewed a salt token into the belly of a red kite, tied its string to one boat's stern, and let it run over the white sea to the other. Tavo the Gale came laughing and tore the cloth at the top, but the string held, and the token dropped into the second boat's hands. The bargain was made. Tavo is still sore he was not asked. Hesk counted the string, out and back, and found it true. So when two boats under the Leeward Reach agree on a price without shouting, the old ones say the Nelu is flying tonight, and a fair trade is a kite that comes home.
output.verse:
Salt sewn in red cloth,
the string runs across white sea,
a fair trade comes home.
